newsitem.title: USA: Greenbrier sees improved freightcar demand.
newsitem.headline: Greenbrier sees improved freightcar demand.

text.p: The Greenbrier Cos Inc said Wednesday it is seeing an improvement in demand for new freightcars as well as in its leasing and trading segments.

"We expect to operate at higher production levels and with a more favorable product mix over the next two quarters, when compared to the prior two quarters," said William Furman, president and chief operating officer, in a press release.
Greenbrier said third-quarter results were affected by lower overall deliveries in a soft car market, an intensely competitive environment, and a less favorable product mix.
The company said it continues to consider ways to improve the financial results of the logistics operations.
In its marine operations, the company received orders for two additional barges. It also said it was unable to conclude contract negotiations on a separate order for two marine barges.
Greenbrier posted third-quarter net income of $0.06 per share on revenues of $96.8 million compared to $0.35 per share on $121.1 million in revenues last year.
